topic: Physical Divisions and Rivers of Uttar Pradesh
description: This topic provides a detailed study of the geographical setup and the river system of Uttar Pradesh. It is an extremely important topic for state-level competitive examinations under State Specific GK.

sections.title: Physical Divisions of Uttar Pradesh
sections.description: The landmass of Uttar Pradesh is primarily divided into three major physical regions based on its geographical features.

key_concepts.explanation: Bhabar is a porous region running parallel to the Shivalik foothills, characterized by pebbles and stones, where streams often disappear underground. To its south lies the Terai, a marshy and moist region famous for dense forests and tall grasses.
A highly fertile plain region formed by the deposition of alluvial soil by the Ganga and its tributaries. It is geologically divided into Bangar (older alluvium) and Khadar (newer alluvium).
This region is the northern extension of Peninsular India. It is commonly known as the Bundelkhand and Baghelkhand plateaus, primarily composed of ancient gneiss and granite rocks.

sections.title: Important Facts regarding Rivers and Geography
sections.description: Highly exam-oriented one-liner facts related to the geography and river systems of Uttar Pradesh.

important_facts.fact: The Ganga river flows through 28 districts of Uttar Pradesh, covering a distance of approximately 1,450 km within the state.
The Yamuna river flows through 19 districts of Uttar Pradesh before merging with the Ganga.
The Chambal river is infamous for its deep ravines or badlands, which are the result of severe gully soil erosion.
The confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna, and the mythical Saraswati rivers takes place in Prayagraj, widely revered as the 'Triveni Sangam'.
The oldest canal of Uttar Pradesh is the Eastern Yamuna Canal, whose construction was completed in the year 1830.
